Hi Mina,

Quick note from NimbusAI — we're finalizing the Singapore launch plan and need a committed dedicated pool for inference that can handle three short daily micro-bursts (each ~12 minutes) with peak concurrency ~220 concurrent sessions and p95 latency <= 120ms.

Attached is a sketch of our traffic pattern and a first-pass compute estimate. Procurement is asking for a firm monthly committed GPU footprint and expected burst allowances to include in the contract.

Can Redwood size a dedicated APAC pool for this and confirm lead times? Also, any recommendations on fallback regions (if SGP capacity is constrained) and whether autoscaling with burst credits would work from a pricing/SLAs perspective.

Thanks — Teresa

Teresa,

Thanks for the note and the attachments — useful detail. High-level answers up front: yes, we can provision a Singapore-dedicated pool sized for those burst windows and we have two common options for burst handling:

- Option A (Recommended): Dedicated steady capacity sized to cover sustained baseline + a burst buffer (reserved burst credits) that gives predictable p95 latency during micro-bursts.
- Option B: Smaller dedicated baseline + cross-region fallback to HK/EU with automated traffic routing; cheaper but introduces regional latency variance.

I'll loop Karthik for a sizing calc and David on procurement/lead-time constraints. Would you be available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Wed 31st) 10:00 SGT? If so I'll send a calendar invite and bring the pool-sizing workbook.

Thanks Mina / Teresa — I reviewed the traffic sample. Quick sizing summary (very conservative initial approach):

- Peak concurrency 220 sessions -> ~6 tokens/sec average per session -> ~1,320 tokens/sec at peak.
- Using our p95 latency target (<=120ms) with the customer's model family (3B dense + small KV), we estimate ~6 A100-equivalent GPUs to sustain the peak if batching is minimal during bursts.
- To allow headroom and maintain SLAs with bursty load, we propose 8 reserved GPU equivalents in the SGP pool, with an additional cross-region burst lane of 4 GPUs (HK) for overflow.

Operational notes:
- Lead time: procurement for dedicated A100-equivalents in SGP is currently ~6–9 weeks for reserved provisioning (due to capacity cadence).
- Alternative short-term plan: temporarily pin 4 dedicated GPUs in SGP and use dedicated burst credits that can scale to 8 for the first 6 weeks while we bring the full pool up. That lets Nimbus go live with tested SLOs.

I've attached a lightweight workbook (I pasted the numbers into the Drive link Mina included). Action items for the call: confirm acceptable risk/price for the temporary burst-credit plan vs waiting for full reserve.

— Karthik

Mina / team — quick procurement and feasibility flags from infra sourcing: we have two important constraints to call out before Nimbus signs a long-term commit.

1) Hardware availability window: SGP region inventories for A100-class hardware are variable; committed time to full 8-GPU pool could be as long as 10–12 weeks if we need to ship/rack new hardware from our vendors. If Nimbus requires contract start aligned with calendar month, we need a plan for week 0..6.

2) Pricing for temporary burst credits: we can offer a burst-credit reservation (prepaid credits redeemable against ephemeral capacity) at a 15% premium to the committed rate. That premium covers the operational overhead to guarantee p95 during burst windows.

Recommendation: go with Karthik's temporary hybrid approach: initial 4 GPUs dedicated + burst credits to the equivalent of +4 GPUs for the first 6 weeks, then convert to 8 dedicated GPUs once SGP inventory is confirmed. That minimizes launch risk.

I'll draft a short procurement note (cost delta + lead time) after the call.

— David

Teresa — thanks for the productive sync earlier today. Confirming the decisions and next steps so procurement has a single reference: 

Summary decisions:
- Launch plan: start with 4 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs in Singapore + prepaid burst credits sized to cover an additional 4-GPU-equivalent for the three daily micro-bursts.
- Go-live contingency: automatic overflow to our HK pool (4 GPUs) if SGP burst capacity is saturated; routing adds ~12–25ms RTT in worst case.
- SLOs: p95 latency target of 120ms during bursts; Redwood will monitor and trigger alerts if we see >2 occurrences/week where p95 >180ms.
- Lead times & conversion: procurement to sign the initial 6-week hybrid plan; Redwood to confirm full 8-GPU committed provisioning timeline within 72 hours of procurement sign-off. Expect 6–9 weeks typical, up to 12 in worst case.
